notes: Check batch for the new log-tests case, skill condition, run on the working tree's uncommitted skill (head 35abbad; the runs' skill copy is identical to the current idiomatic-elixir/ folder): four runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. Every transcript reads SKILL.md, then the input, then references/testing.md with Read, matching reads in result.json; no Skill tool call. Expected reads (testing.md) is met in 4 of 4. No previous grade file exists for this case; the shared testing rules are graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-22-b/grades/test-writing-*.json.

New rule "Capture logs with `capture_log/2`, not a handler": 0 of 4 violate, and no run adds a :logger handler, a StringIO device, a backend, Logger.configure or Logger.put_module_level (the primary-level sentence stays unprovoked, as the index says). Per run: haiku-1 with_log/2 through a helper for every test, options format "[$level] $metadata$message
", metadata [:request_id, :amount_cents], colors disabled; metadata asserted as one exact line (line 42); success absence by refute log =~ ~r/\[(warning|error|critical|alert|emergency)\]/ (line 83) plus a positive info-line assertion. haiku-2 with_log/2 in the three log tests, format "[$level] $metadata$message
", metadata: :all, colors disabled; metadata by three ^\[warning\]-anchored regexes (lines 68-70); success absence by the same refute regex (line 49) after an info-line assertion. sonnet-1 with_log/2 through a helper for every test, format "$level $metadata$message
", metadata [:request_id, :amount_cents], colors disabled; metadata by separate substrings "request_id=req_7" and "amount_cents=4200" (lines 64-65); success absence by an empty capture with [level: :warning] ++ @log_options and assert log == "" (lines 49-51). sonnet-2 capture_log/2 with the asserted call inside, format "$level $metadata$message
", metadata [:request_id, :amount_cents], no colors option; metadata by separate substrings (lines 74-75); success absence by capture_log([level: :warning], ...) and assert log == "" (lines 50-54).

To check that the log assertions are not vacuous, each file was also run against five mutants of the input (success logs at warning, declined logs at info, declined drops amount_cents, request_id metadata removed, unavailable logs at warning instead of error): every file fails at least one test on every mutant, so the empty level: :warning captures and the refute regexes both detect a warning on the success path.

Graded rules changed since 0397dec. "Assert with patterns" gained two sentences: "Put the call under test on the left of `==` and the expected value on the right" (committed) and, uncommitted, "In a test body, put `assert` in front of a match: a bare `{:ok, pid} = start(...)` fails as a `MatchError` without the assertion's formatted value." The second decides this case: 0 of 4 violate, but three runs are clean by judgment. haiku-1 (line 34: {result, _log} = charge_logged("declined", 4_200)), haiku-2 (line 43) and sonnet-1 (line 49) destructure with_log's {result, log} tuple without assert. I read the sentence by its reason, a match on the call's outcome that can fail, and with_log always returns a two-tuple, so these are not the bare-match shape. Reading the sentence literally would make those three runs violated, and both tiers with them, leaving only sonnet-2 clean (log = capture_log(...) with the assert inside, the rule's example shape). haiku-1 also binds result and then asserts a pattern on it (lines 34-36), a two-step shape the rule names only for ==. sonnet-1 shows the one-step form, line 45: assert {{:ok, "ch_123"}, _log} = charge_with_log(ApprovingGateway). No run puts the expected value on the left of ==.

"Group tests by function and name them by behaviour" changed in b0bf52c; the sentence that decides it is "A test's name is the line a failure prints, so it says what the function did in the situation the test sets up: the value it returned, in the domain's words, or the effect it had." 0 of 4 violate. Every describe block is charge/3 plus a condition ("charge/3 when the card is declined"), none joins two functions, and every test names a returned value or what was logged; haiku-1 line 33 "returns the decline" is the tersest name and was graded clean. "Run tests concurrently unless they share global state" and "Replace dependencies at boundaries, through behaviours" are unchanged and clean in 4 of 4: all use async: true, haiku-1 uses one Payments.Gateway module answering by token, and the other three use one module per outcome.

Outside the case's list: haiku-2 breaks "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call". Its return-value tests spread the options keyword list over several lines inside the call (lines 35-39, 55-59, 76-80). sonnet-2 names the same list first with opts = [...]. Not reported: the nested test doubles in haiku-2 and sonnet-1 have no @moduledoc false, but they live in an .exs test script that builds no docs. haiku-1's result variable is a with_log destructure, not one of the names the naming rule lists.

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r log-tests-input.ex charger_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.4, 20 times each with random seeds. Every file passed every time with no compiler warnings: haiku-1 8 tests, the others 6. haiku-2 and sonnet-2 call charge/3 outside any capture in their return-value tests, so each run prints the info, warning and error lines to the console. No current rule text forbids this; the earlier "Other ExUnit features" line that said capture_log checks output "instead of printing it" was removed in this change. All four pass mix format --check-formatted, which confirms format_ok.
